recommendation_summary: Rejects the typed-initials column and naming convention. Recommends keeping the current folder for drafting and adding one 'Released' folder now. Only the three reviewers can write to it and authors can only read it. A reviewer releases a document by saving a frozen copy such as a PDF. The platform's audit log records who released it and when, and a seven-year retention lock stops the copy being changed or deleted. Unmet needs: confirming that the platform's audit log and retention lock actually meet the seven-year requirement, and adding a rule that another reviewer releases any document a reviewer wrote, if that happens.

labels.Requirements and who asked: The customer contract requires that each released document keep its exact approved version, approver identity and approval time for seven years. Authors must not approve their own documents, and later edits must not change the approved version. You need this before this week's delivery.
labels.Deleted: A typed-initials APPROVED column and a naming convention as the control. Anyone with edit access can type anyone's initials, nothing records the time, and an author can still edit the file afterward.
labels.Bottleneck: Authors can write to the same place where approved versions live.
labels.Checked myself: Only what you told me. I have not seen the folder or the platform it runs on.

note: The reply chooses a release folder only reviewers can write to, a frozen copy, the platform audit log and a retention lock. Together these tie a non-author approver and the approval time to the exact version and protect both for the retention period.
